excerpt: ggml-openvino: fix CI op tests and improve KV cache decode (#33002) ggml-openvino: write back consumed in-place nodes of op-test graphs On the naive path every node of an op-test graph is a model output, except an in-place node that another node reads: it got no output, so its destination buffer was never written. GATED_DELTA_NET_CACHE_FUSION copies the final state into the cache and then reads the copy, so the cache kept its old contents. Write such a node back through its view_src, as is already done when nothing reads it. Model graphs are unchanged. ggml-openvino: keep the rest of the buffer in a partial in-place FILL An in-place FILL on a view into part of a larger buffer produced only the filled values. Its output stands for the whole in-place source, so the write-back put those values at the start of the buffer and not at the view's offset. For a contiguous view with a static shape, build the whole buffer: the elements before the view, the filled values, then the elements after it. Add NodeContext::get_inplace_op_src() to detect the in-place case. ggml-openvino: fix softplus precision for large negative inputs softplus was computed as relu(x) + log(1 + exp(-|x|)). When exp(-|x|) is below the precision of 1 + exp(-|x|), the log returns 0 or one ulp, so for x below about -16 in f32 the result was 0 or far off. The SOFTPLUS test case with inputs in [-16.6, -16] fails on CPU and GPU. Compute log1p(y) for y = exp(-|x|) with the series y - y^2/2 + y^3/3 - y^4/4 when y < 0.01, where its relative error is below 2e-9, and keep log(1 + y) above that. ggml-openvino: finer GPU KV rounding for decode batches Rounding the GPU KV length up to a power of two makes a batch attend up to twice the rows that hold data right after each power of two. Decode reads every attended row, so long contexts lose decode speed. The GPU plugin keeps memory for each attended length: several large buffers for a prompt batch, about one copy of K and V for a decode batch. Keep the power of two…
